candidates.support: Tyre, on the coast of the South Governorate of Lebanon, is undisputed in identity and location; Pleiades and Wikidata's coordinates for the site agree closely.

summary.text: Tyre was, per UNESCO, 'the great Phoenician city that reigned over the seas,' founding colonies such as Carthage and controlling much of the ancient Mediterranean's maritime trade. Jesus withdrew into the region of Tyre and Sidon and healed a Gentile woman's daughter there, and on his final journey to Jerusalem Paul's ship put in at Tyre, where he found and stayed with disciples for seven days before continuing to Ptolemais.

otConnections.note: Ezekiel pronounces a lengthy oracle of judgment against Tyre for its role in ancient Mediterranean trade, one of the Old Testament's most extensive prophecies against a single foreign city.

Hiram, king of Tyre, supplies King Solomon with cedar and craftsmen for the building of the Jerusalem temple, an alliance the New Testament's Gospel references to Tyre and Sidon presuppose as long-standing regional neighbors of Israel.
